settings.oidc_duplicate_provider: Each provider and domain or issuer can only be configured once.
settings.oidc_keep_secret: Leave blank to keep the saved secret.
settings.oidc_no_providers: No NS8 OIDC providers are available.
settings.oidc_no_domains: No user domains are available for this provider.
settings.oidc_invalid_issuer: Enter a valid HTTPS issuer URL.
settings.oidc_registration_failed: Warpgate could not register with this provider.
settings.title: Settings
settings.host_pattern: Must be a valid fully qualified domain name
settings.host_format: Must be a valid fully qualified domain name
settings.database_help: Warpgate stores users, targets and sessions in a database. Choose the built-in SQLite file, or a PostgreSQL database to share it between several Warpgate instances.
settings.database_no_instances: Install PostgreSQL 19c from the Software Center to use a PostgreSQL database.
settings.database_instance_auto: Choose for me (the one on this node first)
settings.cluster_help: Several Warpgate instances can share one PostgreSQL database, with the same users, targets and SSH host key.
settings.cluster_create: Let other instances join this one
settings.peer_approvals_help: An instance can join only after you allow it here.
settings.vault_help: Keep a copy of the database password and other secrets in OpenBao. Warpgate still starts from its local copy.
settings.vault_provisioned: Get access from an OpenBao instance of this cluster
settings.vault_status_pending: Waiting for the OpenBao administrator to approve the request.
settings.vault_status_stale: The approval was for an earlier installation with the same name. Request access again.
settings.vault_token_keep: Leave empty to keep the saved token
settings.openbao_request_failed: The request could not be sent to OpenBao.
settings.cannot_switch_to_embedded: An instance using PostgreSQL cannot go back to SQLite.
settings.cluster_requires_postgresql: A cluster needs a PostgreSQL database.
settings.cannot_join_from_create: Other instances depend on this one: it cannot join another.
settings.postgresql19c_instance_not_found: This PostgreSQL instance is no longer available.
settings.peer_not_approved: The other instance has not allowed this one to join.
settings.invalid_url: Enter an http or https address.
settings.cluster_join_password: Users live in the shared database: after joining, sign in to this instance with the admin password of the instance that created the cluster. The password generated for this instance is no longer used.
settings.recordings_help: Where Warpgate keeps session recordings. Turn recording on or off in the Warpgate administration interface.
settings.recordings_local: Local disk (data volume of this instance)
settings.recordings_inherited: This instance uses the recordings storage of {peer}. Change it there, then save the settings of each member again.
settings.recordings_cluster_local: With local storage, a finished recording can be replayed only from the cluster member that recorded it. Use an S3 bucket to replay recordings from any member.
settings.recordings_endpoint_help: Leave empty for Amazon S3. Browsers download recordings from this address: it must be reachable over HTTPS by the people who replay them.
settings.recordings_path_style: Path-style addressing (needed by most S3-compatible services)
settings.recordings_keep_secret: Leave blank to keep the saved secret key.
settings.recordings_http_endpoint: Browsers block recordings downloaded over plain HTTP from the HTTPS administration page: replay may not work.
settings.recordings_s3_notes: Warpgate 0.30 has no option to skip TLS verification: the endpoint needs a certificate trusted by a public authority. The secret key is kept in a private file of this module and passed to Warpgate in its environment, not in its database or configuration file.
settings.recordings_migration: Switching storage does not move existing recordings. After switching to S3, recordings already on the local disk stay there but cannot be replayed from Warpgate, unless you copy the recordings folder of the data volume into the bucket under the same prefix. After switching back to local disk, recordings in the bucket cannot be replayed.
settings.recordings_test_ok: The bucket is reachable with these credentials.
settings.s3_wrong_region: The bucket is in another region.
settings.s3_unreachable: The endpoint cannot be reached from this node.
settings.s3_tls_error: The endpoint certificate is not trusted.
settings.s3_bad_request: The endpoint rejected the request. Check the region and addressing style.
settings.s3_invalid_endpoint: Enter an http or https URL with a host name and optional port, without a path.
settings.s3_invalid_region: Enter a region name, like us-east-1.
settings.s3_invalid_bucket: Use 3 to 63 lowercase letters, digits, dots and hyphens, starting and ending with a letter or digit.
settings.s3_dotted_bucket_needs_path_style: A bucket name with dots needs path-style addressing over HTTPS.
settings.s3_invalid_prefix: Use letters, digits and !_.*'()/- without empty, "." or ".." parts.
settings.s3_invalid_access_key: The access key ID cannot contain spaces.
settings.s3_invalid_secret: The secret key cannot contain spaces or line breaks.
settings.invalid_peer_recordings: The other instance sent invalid recordings storage settings.
settings.vault_unseal: Configure automatic or transit unseal for the OpenBao instance that Warpgate uses: a sealed OpenBao cannot serve target credentials after a restart until someone unseals it.
settings.secret_backend_help: Warpgate can read target credentials and sign SSH certificates with an OpenBao server, using secret:// references.
settings.secret_backend_off: Off: manage secret backends in Warpgate yourself
settings.secret_backend_manual: Manual: show the values to enter in Warpgate
settings.secret_backend_managed: Managed: register it with a token from OpenBao
settings.secret_backend_requires_provisioning: Managed mode needs the OpenBao section set to get access from an OpenBao instance of this cluster.
settings.secret_backend_managed_by_creator: In a cluster, the instance that created it manages the secret backend for all members.
settings.secret_backend_scope_group: Secrets of a shared group approved in OpenBao
settings.secret_backend_group_help: Ask the OpenBao administrator to approve this module for the group.
settings.secret_backend_module_scope: The module token can also read this module's copy of its own secrets in OpenBao. Warpgate restricts references to the targets path, but enable the database encryption key so the token is stored encrypted, or use a shared group.

settings.secret_backend_invalid_name: Use 1 to 64 letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens.
settings.secret_backend_invalid_group: A group ID has lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, and ends with a letter.
settings.secret_backend_group_not_approved: OpenBao has not approved this module for the group.
settings.secret_backend_no_token: No OpenBao token is available yet.
settings.client_not_approved: OpenBao has not approved this module yet.
